newsitem.title: USA: Citgo sees only Lake Charles refinery repair delay.
newsitem.headline: Citgo sees only Lake Charles refinery repair delay.

text.p: CITGO Petroleum Corp said Friday that it plans no further initiatives for its refineries in order to comply with an Energy Department request to boost distillate output.

CITGO executives said last Friday after a meeting with Energy Secretary O'Leary that maintenance at the 32,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) hydrocracking unit at its Lake Charles plant would be postponed to help alleviate a shortage of distillate.
The refinery has a rated capacity to process 320,000 barrels of crude a day.
"Apart from delaying a hydrocracker maintenance at Lake Charles we've got nothing," said Kent Young, a CITGO spokesman.

Meanwhile, CITGO's joint venture plant with Lyondell Petrochemical Co in Houston -- the 265,000 bpd Lyondell-CITGO Refining Co plant -- said it expects its 102,000 bpd fluid catalytic cracker (FCC) unit to be back up on schedule in the second week of November after scheduled maintenance which began at the end of September.
But there is no special reconfiguration of the plant planned in order to boost distillate output, according to spokesperson Kathleen Abel.
Lyondell, announcing its third quarter results last Monday, said the FCC turnaround and weak industry refining margins "is expected to have a negative impact on LCR's results in the fourth quarter."

The Lyondell-CITGO Houston plant has been subject to a $1.1 billion expansion project dating from late 1994 and due for completion when a new 45,000 bpd coker unit is added in the first quarter of 1997.

The project is aimed at increasing the plant's ability to process heavier-grade crudes. It can process 130,000 bpd of 22 degree (API) crude but will be able to process 200,000 bpd of heavier 17 degree (API) oil after completion.
This is to fit with LCR's 25-year crude supply deal with LAGOVEN, an affiliate of Venezuelan state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela, CITGO ultimate parent.
